metadata.title: Claude, Cowork Plugin Customizer.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether a Claude Skill named cowork-plugin-customizer is a plugin Claude has installed, or something else, using the skill's own one stated job -- customize a Claude Code plugin for one organization's tools -- as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that a Skill is a file Claude reads, not software it installs, and that the repeatability guarantee only covers what the file wrote down.
metadata.anchor_pair: B01 -> B03 (cowork-plugin-customizer's one stated job-line, planted inside the folder/SKILL.md reveal, paid off by the same line still governing the steps -- and where a request can step past them)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes cowork-plugin-customizer is a plugin Claude installs, like an app. It isn't — it's a skill folder Claude actually reads. So what does reading it, instead of installing it, really mean?

beats.act: 1 stakes / 2 wrong guess, falsified / 4 ANCHOR PLANTED
beats.narration_text: A Claude Skill is a folder, not an installed program. Inside, a file named SKILL.md — plain-language instructions, no hidden binary. Claude opens that file before it does anything else. cowork-plugin-customizer is one such folder: its whole job, written in one line inside that file, is to customize a Claude Code plugin for one organization's tools.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — a folder opening to reveal SKILL.md, the one job-line typing itself out

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — a folder, a file, one job-line
production_viz.mechanic: A plain folder icon labelled 'cowork-plugin-customizer' opens on cream. Inside it a single file card reading 'SKILL.md' fades in. THE ANCHOR. Beneath the filename, one line of text types itself out letter by letter: 'Customize a Claude Code plugin for one organization's tools.' No binary icon, no gear, no install progress bar anywhere in frame. THIS EXACT JOB-LINE RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Reading it is only step one. Claude then works through whatever Steps section the file lays out, top to bottom, in order — no branching unless a step explicitly says so. For cowork-plugin-customizer, that means the same request runs the same sequence every time; nothing about what happens in between is left to guesswork.

shot.new_visual_element: A numbered Steps list drawing in top to bottom, a loop arrow marked 'same request, same order'

production_viz.label: Top to bottom, in order
production_viz.mechanic: A numbered list card labelled 'Steps' draws in one line at a time, top to bottom, each numbered line appearing only after the one above it settles — no two lines ever appear out of order. Once the list is complete, a looping arrow wraps around the whole card with a small label: 'same request, same order.' The arrow completes one full loop and holds.

beats.narration_text: That's the guarantee: read the file, and you can predict the run before it starts, because the steps are sitting right there in plain language. But the guarantee only covers what's written. Ask for something the Steps section never anticipated, and Claude isn't wrong to attempt it — it just isn't following cowork-plugin-customizer anymore. It's using its own judgment, off the map the file drew.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the SKILL.md job-line reappears inside its steps, then a request steps off the edge of the drawn steps into open, unmarked space

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — on the map, then off it
production_viz.mechanic: THE B01 JOB-LINE RETURNS, identical, now sitting at the top of the B02 numbered Steps card — the same words, this time governing a visible sequence. A single request marker travels down the steps in order, staying on the drawn path. Then a second request marker appears and walks straight off the right edge of the card into blank cream — no steps drawn there, no error mark, just open space. A caption beneath reads: 'off the map the file drew.'

beats.narration_text: A Skill isn't installed software — it's a file Claude reads before it acts. Same request gets the same steps every time, but only for what that file actually wrote down.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Then run it, and check whether it followed the order it just showed you. Liam, in for Bear.
